html:
In January 2022 protests over fuel prices in Kazakhstan turned into the worst violence in the country since independence, and into a struggle for power at the top.

On 1 January the government lifted a price cap on liquefied gas, which many Kazakhs use to run their cars. The price doubled. Protests began peacefully in the oil town of Zhanaozen and spread across the country. In Almaty, the largest city, armed crowds stormed and burned the city hall and took the airport.

President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev called in troops of the Russian-led Collective Security Treaty Organization and ordered security forces to shoot to kill without warning. More than 200 people died and thousands were arrested.

Behind the street violence lay a fight among the elite. Tokayev removed Nursultan Nazarbayev, the former president, from his last post as head of the Security Council, and the head of national security was arrested for treason. Nazarbayev's relatives lost their positions, and a new constitutional reform followed that year.
sum: In January 2022 protests over fuel prices in Kazakhstan turned into the worst violence in the country since independence, and into a struggle for power at the top.
